answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-weighted reputation. Each agent locks a refundable deposit before entering a task market, and a mirror of its work history lets independent auditors verify it, so a fresh identity starts at zero trust. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs capital per identity, while honest agents earn reputation over time. When auditors spot a violet-flagged pattern — many new identities funded from one source — they share the evidence across the meadow of verifiers and slash the deposits of coordinated fakes, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
